paragraphs: Rav Mesharshiya, son of Rav Hiyya.
He is mentioned in [Bava Batra 82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.82a.1-2), after the words of Rav Ashi. Perhaps it should read "son of Rav Aha," and "Hiyya" arose from the word "Aha."[^1][^2]

notes.text: The linked Gemara and [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2571&lang=en) name Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Hiyya. The Gemara records his explanation immediately after Rav Ashi’s, after a question posed to Rav Ashi by Rav Acha son of Rav Avya. Hyman’s wording describes the order on the page.

Hyman tentatively proposes Aha in place of Hiyya and suggests the direction Aha→Hiyya for the presumed corruption. His “perhaps” is preserved; the heading and father’s name remain unchanged. The printed פב. is rendered Bava Batra 82a.
